experiment: Standard (AISI) pullover coupon tests, simulated single-panel component pullover tests (concentric, two eccentric conditions, fixed-end) and full-scale vacuum-box system tests were run on 24 and 26 gage Pascoe (Fy = 55 ksi) and American (Fy = 80 ksi) through-fastened roof panels attached with #12 self-drilling screws, with fastener loads, panel displacements, chamber pressure and strains recorded to failure and compared with a derived biaxial membrane pullover theory.
title: Pullover Strength of Self-Drilling Screw Fasteners in Through-Fastened Metal Roof Systems

variables.definition: Test or specimen number identifying each pullover, component or vacuum-box test.
variables.name: Test number
variables.note: Numbers restart within each table and some are letters (A, B, C) in Table 4-3.

variables.definition: Number of the planned test series in the proposed testing program matrix.
variables.name: Test series number
variables.note: Series numbers 1-6 repeat for component and system installations.

variables.definition: Whether the planned tests were component (single panel) or system (multi-panel) installations.
variables.name: Installation type

variables.definition: Supplier of the panel sheet steel (Pascoe, American or Dean), given as a column value or as a column heading in the transposed tables.
variables.evidence: Table 1-1 p. 20; Table 2-1 p. 23; Table 4-8 p. 55; Tables 7-1 to 7-6 pp. 174-175; Table S1 pp. 99-111; Figures 7-6/7-7 p. 196
variables.name: Panel steel supplier
variables.note: In Tables 2-1 and 7-2 the supplier appears as part of the column name (e.g. pascoe_24ga).

variables.definition: Sheet gage designation of the roof panel tested (24 or 26 gage).
variables.evidence: Tables 3-1 to 3-7, Tables 4-1 to 4-8, Table 1-1, Table S1
variables.name: Panel sheet gage
variables.note: Gage entries in Table 1-1 are printed with irregular spacing ('24& 26').

variables.definition: Nominal yield grade of the panel steel (55 ksi Pascoe, 80 ksi American grade E) as printed in the test program and test-table headings.
variables.name: Nominal panel steel grade

variables.definition: Number of tests planned in each series of the proposed testing program.
variables.name: Number of planned tests

variables.definition: Measured thickness of the tensile coupon taken from each panel sheet, averaged per ASTM A370 testing.
variables.name: Coupon sheet thickness
variables.note: 24 ga Pascoe printed as 0.0234 in. but 0.0239 in. is used in the Chapter 7 calculations.

variables.definition: Ultimate load carried by the tensile coupon.
variables.name: Coupon ultimate load

variables.definition: Elongation of the coupon measured at the ultimate load.
variables.name: Coupon elongation at ultimate
variables.note: Pascoe values (~1.24 in.) are orders of magnitude larger than American values (~0.011 in.) as printed.

variables.definition: Load at yield recorded in the tensile coupon test.
variables.name: Coupon yield load

variables.definition: Width of the reduced section of the tensile coupon.
variables.name: Coupon reduced-section width

variables.definition: Cross-sectional area of the reduced section of the tensile coupon.
variables.name: Coupon reduced-section area

variables.definition: Percent reduction of coupon cross-sectional area at fracture.
variables.name: Coupon area reduction

variables.definition: Percent elongation of the tensile coupon.
variables.name: Coupon percent elongation

variables.definition: Measured yield stress of each panel sheet from the tensile coupon test.
variables.evidence: Table 2-1 (yield stress row), p. 23; cited in the table note (26 ga Pascoe 59300 psi, 24 ga Pascoe 50600 psi)
variables.name: Measured yield stress
variables.note: 26 ga Pascoe yield printed higher than 24 ga Pascoe.

variables.definition: Measured ultimate tensile stress of each panel sheet from the tensile coupon test.
variables.name: Measured ultimate tensile stress

variables.definition: Ultimate load carried by a single #12 self-drilling screw in the standard (AISI) pullover coupon test, also listed in ascending order in the companion normal-distribution tables.
variables.evidence: Tables 3-1, 3-3, 3-5, 3-7, 3-9 and the sorted columns of Tables 3-2, 3-4, 3-6, 3-8, pp. 28-38
variables.name: Standard pullover test ultimate load
variables.note: Column name tl_load_lbs is reused in Tables 4-1/4-2 for the load on two fasteners.

variables.definition: Standardized normal variate (Z, printed as 'composita') computed for each sorted standard-test load to screen outliers.
variables.name: Standardized normal variate Z
variables.note: Rejection region taken as |Z| >= 1.96.

variables.definition: Deviation of an individual test load from the series mean, expressed as a percentage.
variables.name: Percent deviation from series mean
variables.note: Preliminary tests show '*' instead of a number.

variables.definition: Observed failure mode and remarks for each test (pullover, pullout, panel buckling, eccentric loading marked '*').
variables.evidence: Comments columns of Tables 3-1 to 3-7 and 4-1/4-2; failure_mode and comments_as_printed in Table S1
variables.name: Failure mode and test comments
variables.note: Multi-line printed comments were joined into one string.

variables.definition: Screw arrangement in the simulated component tests: F = one screw in the centre of each outer valley, C = two screws in the centre valley.
variables.evidence: Tables 4-1, 4-2 and 4-8, pp. 43-55 (header notes define F and C)
variables.name: Screw arrangement

variables.definition: Simulated or clear span length of the panel between supports in the component and vacuum-box tests.
variables.evidence: Tables 4-1, 4-2, 4-4 to 4-8 (inches, pp. 43-55); Table S1 (feet, pp. 99-111)
variables.name: Panel span length
variables.note: Reported in inches for component tests and in feet for the vacuum-box system tests; Test 20/21 prints '21 & 17'.

variables.definition: Total load applied to the two fasteners of the simulated component specimen at failure (also the applied load at each strain-gage reading).
variables.evidence: Tables 4-1, 4-2 (tl_load_lbs, pp. 43-44), Table 4-3 (total_load_lbs, p. 45), Tables 4-4/4-5 (total_load_lbs, pp. 47-49), Table 4-10 (t_load_lbs, p. 65)
variables.name: Total load on two fasteners at failure
variables.note: Tests 20/21 of Table 4-2 print approximate values ('Apx. 1500').

variables.definition: Load carried per screw at failure, obtained by dividing the total specimen load by two.
variables.name: Load per screw at failure

variables.definition: Offset of the screws from the panel centre line in eccentric loading condition 1.
variables.name: Screw offset from panel centre line
variables.note: Eccentric condition 1 is illustrated in Figure 4-3.

variables.definition: Actual distance from the fastener to the fixed boundary when the panel supports were offset (eccentric condition 2).
variables.name: Fastener-to-fixed-boundary distance
variables.note: Eccentric condition 2 is illustrated in Figure 4-4.

variables.definition: Peak load recorded at each of the two instrumented fasteners (larger and smaller value of the pair) in the eccentric and fixed-end component tests, in the system-test summaries and in Table 7-2.
variables.evidence: Tables 4-6, 4-7, 4-8 (pp. 51-55); Table 7-2 p. 174; Table S1 fastener_peak_loads_lb pp. 99-111
variables.name: Fastener peak load
variables.note: An asterisk marks the fastener that failed; Table 7-2 entries carry a loading-type code (e, e*, c).

variables.definition: Deflection measured at the left and right fastener in the earlier Dean-steel component tests.
variables.name: Deflection at fastener
variables.note: Underlining identifying the failed fastener could not be captured.

variables.definition: Rate at which load was applied in the earlier Dean-steel component tests.
variables.name: Rate of load application
variables.note: Test 10 (84.5 lbs/sec) is an order of magnitude above the others.

variables.definition: In-plane strain recorded by each of twelve strain gages on a 24 gage Pascoe panel as load was applied to pullover.
variables.evidence: Table 4-10, p. 65; gage layout in Figure 4-19
variables.name: Panel strain gage reading
variables.note: From the seventh row on only eleven values are printed; the missing gage is unconfirmed.

variables.definition: Load applied to each purpose-built aluminium load cell during calibration.
variables.name: Load cell calibration load
variables.note: Thirteen load levels printed although 'No. of Observations = 25'.

variables.definition: Millivolt output of each of the eight 2024-T4 aluminium load cells at each calibration load.
variables.name: Load cell millivolt output
variables.note: Cell 001 reading at 1000 lb breaks the monotonic trend; column alignment of the regression block is uncertain.

variables.definition: Linear regression output for each load cell calibration (constant, standard error of Y estimate, R squared, number of observations, degrees of freedom, X coefficient and standard error of coefficient), printed as the last seven rows of the calibration table.
variables.name: Load cell calibration regression stats
variables.note: Only seven sets of values are printed for eight cells; the omitted cell appears to be Cell 005.

variables.definition: Calendar date and clock time of each data scan in the vacuum-box time histories.
variables.name: Scan date and time
variables.note: Rows are sampled roughly every 2 s although logging was at 0.25 s intervals.

variables.definition: Panel displacement measured by LVDT 1 and LVDT 2 during the vacuum-box tests, both as a time history and as the value at each fastener failure.
variables.evidence: Tables 4-12 to 4-23 (lvdt1_in, lvdt2_in, pp. 87-98); Table S1 peak_lvdt columns, pp. 99-111
variables.name: Panel displacement (LVDT)
variables.note: Some values print 'NA' in the summary blocks.

variables.definition: Negative chamber pressure recorded by the pressure transducer at each scan of the vacuum-box tests.
variables.name: Chamber pressure time history
variables.note: Several cells were extracted with a space in place of the decimal point.

variables.definition: Individual fastener load recorded by each aluminium load cell at each scan of the vacuum-box tests.
variables.name: Fastener load from load cell
variables.note: Load cells 5 and 8 were lost/locked in several tests and print large negative values.

variables.definition: Governing (largest printed) negative chamber pressure in the summary block of each vacuum-box test, taken as the system uplift capacity, together with the pressure at each listed fastener failure.
variables.evidence: Table S1 failure_load_as_printed and peak_pressures_psi, pp. 99-111
variables.name: Peak chamber pressure at failure
variables.note: Peak values must be taken from the summary block, not from the sampled time-history rows.

variables.definition: Load-cell numbers at which a fastener failure (pullover or pullout) was recorded in each vacuum-box test.
variables.name: Failed load cell numbers
variables.note: Tests 8-10 print the first failed cell as '3#'.

variables.definition: Elapsed duration of each vacuum-box test as printed in the summary block (mm:ss).
variables.name: Elapsed test duration

variables.definition: Number of spans in the vacuum-box test assembly (one or two).
variables.name: Number of spans

variables.definition: Number of purlin support lines in the vacuum-box assembly, where stated.
variables.name: Number of purlin lines
variables.note: Stated only for Test 2.

variables.definition: Panel-to-purlin attachment type for the roof system tested (through-fastened).
variables.name: Panel attachment type

variables.definition: Direction of the applied load on the roof system (uplift produced by chamber vacuum) and the bracing provided to supports and panels.
variables.evidence: Table S1 load_direction and bracing columns, pp. 99-111
variables.name: Load direction and bracing
variables.note: Bracing stated only for some tests.

variables.definition: Flat half-width of the rib top measured from the rib centreline on the dimensioned panel rib profile.
variables.name: Rib top half width
variables.note: Read from the dimensioned figure.

variables.definition: Horizontal projection of the sloping rib web on the dimensioned panel rib profile.
variables.name: Rib web horizontal projection

variables.definition: Vertical height of the panel rib from valley to rib top.
variables.name: Rib height

variables.definition: Length of the sloping rib web measured along the web.
variables.name: Rib web slant length

variables.definition: Horizontal reference length measured from the rib centreline used as l_o in the transverse strain calculation.
variables.name: Transverse reference length l_o

variables.definition: Maximum transverse extension available from flattening the rib, taken as web slant length minus web horizontal projection.
variables.name: Maximum rib flattening delta_max

variables.definition: Transverse membrane strain of the panel at the knee and at the ultimate point of the bilinear transverse stress-strain model (delta_max / l_o at ultimate); also appears as input in the design spreadsheets.
variables.evidence: Figures 7-6/7-7 p. 196 (boxed values); Data Input rows of Tables 7-7 to 7-14 and the note to Table 7-12
variables.name: Transverse strain eps_beta
variables.note: Table 7-12 uses dummy values (9999, 8888) to model a free edge.

variables.definition: Transverse membrane stress of the panel at the knee and at the ultimate strain of the bilinear transverse model, and the transverse stress values used in the design spreadsheets.
variables.evidence: Figures 7-6/7-7 p. 196 (axis labels, two comma-separated values each); notes to Tables 7-12 and 7-14
variables.name: Transverse stress F_beta
variables.note: The figures do not say which of the two printed values belongs to which gage; Table 7-14 prints 97.4 ksi where Table 7-10 uses 10.5 ksi.

variables.definition: Average load capacity of a self-drilling screw from the simulated component tests, tabulated by loading condition (concentric, eccentric condition 1, eccentric condition 2, fixed-end concentric) and used as the measured component strength in the theory comparison.
variables.evidence: Table 7-1 p. 174; component_test_pullover_strength_lb in Table 7-5 p. 175
variables.name: Average component test fastener capacity
variables.note: Dean 26 ga has a value only for the concentric column; the fixed-end and eccentric-1 values were judged unsuitable for the reduction factor.

variables.definition: Mean fastener pullover strength measured in the vacuum-box system tests for each panel type (average of the peak loads of Table 7-2).
variables.evidence: Table 7-6 p. 175; averages rows of Table 7-2 p. 174
variables.name: Mean system test pullover strength

variables.definition: Mean pullover strength measured in the standard (uniaxial concentric) AISI test for each panel type, used as the reference strength in the comparisons.
variables.name: Mean standard test pullover strength

variables.definition: Reduction factor to be applied to the Standard Pullover Test / AISI Equation E4.4.2.1 strength, derived from the component and from the system test capacities.
variables.name: Pullover strength reduction factor
variables.note: The lowest system-test factor (0.235) is the recommended value.

variables.definition: Pullover strength predicted by the derived Chapter 5 biaxial membrane theory, reported in pounds in the comparison tables and as Pnov in kips in the Step 7 row of the design spreadsheets.
variables.evidence: Tables 7-4, 7-5, 7-6 p. 175; Step 7 rows and header notes of Tables 7-7 to 7-14, pp. 184-191
variables.name: Predicted pullover strength Pnov
variables.note: Pnov values range from 0.234779 to 1.009245 kips; the 24 ga American component case differs from test by 79.7%.

variables.definition: Percent difference between the measured pullover strength and the theoretical prediction.
variables.name: Percent error of prediction
variables.note: Two American grade E component cases show 79.741% and 45.109%.

variables.definition: Name of each printed spreadsheet parameter and the calculation block (Data Input, Step 1 ... Step 7) it belongs to in the design-procedure sheets.
variables.name: Design calculation parameter label
variables.note: Greek symbols are written out; Λ is the printed symbol for the deflection Δ.

variables.definition: Longitudinal (along-rib) distance from the fastener to the panel boundary, maximum and minimum, entered as Lαmax and Lαmin in the design spreadsheets.
variables.evidence: Data Input rows of Tables 7-7 to 7-14, pp. 184-191
variables.name: Longitudinal distance L_alpha
variables.note: Values are 6.5-24.6 in. depending on the test modelled.

variables.definition: Transverse (across-rib) distance from the fastener to the panel boundary, maximum and minimum, entered as Lβmax and Lβmin in the design spreadsheets.
variables.evidence: Data Input rows of Tables 7-7 to 7-14, pp. 184-191
variables.name: Transverse distance L_beta

variables.definition: Washer-to-hole geometry ratio (dw+dh)/(dw-dh) evaluated in Step 6 of the design spreadsheets from the screw washer diameter dw and the panel hole diameter dh.
variables.evidence: Step 6 rows of Tables 7-7 to 7-14; note to Table 7-10, p. 187
variables.name: Washer/hole diameter ratio
variables.note: Table 7-10 prints the ratio as (dw+dh)/(dα-dh), apparently a typographical error.

variables.definition: Transverse deflection term Λβ (printed Λ for Δ) computed in the design spreadsheets, e.g. Λβminu = 172000 in for the free-edge model.
variables.evidence: Design-procedure rows of Tables 7-7 to 7-14; note to Table 7-12, p. 189
variables.name: Transverse deflection Lambda_beta
variables.note: Free-edge case uses a dummy very large value.

variables.definition: Elastic and plastic transverse moduli (Eeβ, Epβ) of the bilinear transverse stress-strain model used in the design spreadsheets.
variables.evidence: Design-procedure rows of Tables 7-7 to 7-14; note to Table 7-12 (Eeβmin = 0.000743 ksi, Epβmin = 0.053465 ksi), p. 189
variables.name: Transverse moduli Ee_beta and Ep_beta
variables.note: Free-edge case uses near-zero dummy moduli.
